label: EU(7)-PIM: fluoxetine, paroxetine, fluvoxamine
title: Fluoxetine, paroxetine or fluvoxamine in an older person
statement: Fluoxetine | In lists: 3, 4 (A); 2, 5, 6 (B) | Main reason: CNS side effects (nausea, insomnia, dizziness, confusion); hyponatremia | Dose adjustment/special considerations: Reduce dose; start with 20 mg/d; maximum dose also 20 mg/d; avoid administration at bedtime. E, M | Alternatives: Non-pharmacological treatment, SSRI (except PIM: fluoxetine, paroxetine, fluvoxamine)[e], mirtazapine[d], trazodone. E || Paroxetine | In lists: 2, 5, 6 (B) | Main reason: Higher risk of all-cause mortality, higher risk of seizures, falls and fractures. Anticholinergic adverse effects | Dose adjustment/special considerations: For older adults or for patients with renal failure, start immediate-release tablets with 10 mg/d (12.5 mg/d if controlled-release tablets), increased by 10 mg/d (12.5 mg/d if controlled-release tablets), up to 40 mg/d (50 mg/d if controlled-release tablets). E, M | Alternatives: Non-pharmacological treatment, SSRI (except PIM: fluoxetine, paroxetine, fluvoxamine)[e], mirtazapine[d], trazodone. E || Fluvoxamine | In lists: 2, 5, 6 (B) | Main reason: Higher risk of all-cause mortality, self-harm, falls, fractures and hyponatraemia | Dose adjustment/special considerations: Reduce dose for older adults and patients with renal failure; start with 50-100 mg/d; titrate slowly. E, M | Alternatives: Non-pharmacological treatment, SSRI (except PIM: fluoxetine, paroxetine, fluvoxamine)[e], mirtazapine[d], trazodone. E

plain_summary: Three antidepressants (fluoxetine, paroxetine and fluvoxamine) are on a European list of medicines to avoid or use at a lower dose in older people, because of falls, low sodium and other side effects.

medicine_groups.name: Fluoxetine, paroxetine and fluvoxamine (antidepressants)
medicine_groups.note: Tablets, capsules and liquids count. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too. The list is for older people, so the rule uses age 65 or over.

rule_for_models: Suspect a finding when a person aged 65 or over is supplied any Group A medicine (fluoxetine, paroxetine or fluvoxamine). If age is unknown and a Group A medicine is supplied, report only a possible finding and ask the pharmacist to confirm whether the person is at least 65. Work out the daily dose from the strength and directions. If directions do not establish a daily dose, keep the age-eligible supply finding, state that the dose is unknown and ask how much the patient takes each day. Leave the higher-dose concern unconfirmed. A fluoxetine dose above 20 mg a day, or a paroxetine dose above 40 mg a day (50 mg a day if controlled release), is a stronger sign.
cannot_be_seen: Why the antidepressant was started, how well it works, sodium and kidney blood test results, falls, and what the person really takes.
ask_the_gp: A review of whether this antidepressant and dose are still the best choice for this person, and whether a sodium blood test is due.
